subject: Architecture
title: Greek Classical: Where It All Began
description: One-minute skill: Greek Classical: Where It All Began.

hook.text: The ancient Greeks invented three column styles that the entire Western world still copies today.

buildup.text: Doric columns are plain and sturdy. Ionic ones have scrolls. Corinthian ones sprout acanthus leaves.

discovery.text: Greek temples used 'entasis' — a slight curve in columns that makes them look perfectly straight.

twist.text: The buildings weren't white marble. Bright paint covered them in reds, blues, and golds.

climax.text: Every government building with columns, from Washington to Berlin, quotes Greek architecture.

punchline.text: Democracy invented the column. The column still means democracy.

quiz.question: What is 'entasis' in Greek architecture?
options: A type of decorative frieze on temple roofs
A slight curve in columns to make them appear straight
A method of joining marble blocks without mortar

details.summary: Greek Classical architecture established the foundational principles of Western building — proportion, symmetry, and the column orders (Doric, Ionic, Corinthian). Born in the 5th century BCE, these ideals have been recycled in every era since, from Roman temples to modern courthouses.
details.whyItMatters: Nearly every public building you walk past owes something to Greek Classical design. Understanding its principles reveals why columns, pediments, and proportional harmony persist across 2,500 years of architecture.
takeaways: Greek architecture introduced Doric, Ionic, and Corinthian orders
Proportion and symmetry were its core design principles
Its influence persists in Western public buildings today

faq.question: What are the three Greek column orders?
faq.answer: Doric is the simplest with no base and plain capitals. Ionic adds scrolled volutes at the capital. Corinthian is the most ornate with acanthus leaf carvings. Each order carried cultural meaning — Doric suggested strength, Ionic grace, Corinthian luxury.

faq.question: Why do modern government buildings still use Greek columns?
faq.answer: Greek architecture became associated with democracy, reason, and civic virtue. When democratic nations like the United States needed a visual language for governance, they borrowed Greek forms to signal those values — a tradition that continues today.
